blocks.text: VPN access policy rules enable you to allow or block network traffic on VPN Service Edges. Before you configure an access policy rule, configure the components that define the traffic's source and destination:

blocks.item: For the source, you can define rules based on user identity by configuring client IP pools that are mapped to identity provider (IdP) attributes.

For the destination, consider configuring IP address objects and grouping Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) blocks, IP addresses, and FQDNs that can be used in multiple policy rules to help organize network resources.

blocks.text: VPN access policy rules provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Enforce identity-based access by creating rules based on user attributes from your IdP such as department and group.
Allow or block network traffic on VPN Service Edges.
Restrict access based on configured address books.

blocks.text: VPN (for Legacy Apps) evaluates access policy rules using a top-down, specific-match principle. Traffic that doesn't match any access policy rule is blocked by default. If you are new to VPN (for Legacy Apps), you must create a policy rule to allow traffic through the VPN tunnel.
On the Access Policies page (Private Access > VPN (for Legacy Apps) > VPN Access Policy > Access Policies), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Hide or show filters for the page.
Search for an access policy rule by its name.
Add a new access policy rule.
Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. Click Clear to remove the applied filters.
View a list of all configured access policy rules. For each rule, you can see:

Rule Order: The policy evaluation order number for the rule. Rules are evaluated using a top-down, specific-match principle. You can change the rule order by clicking the number and manually entering a new value.
Name: The name of the rule.
Source Networks: The source networks from where the traffic originates.
Source Ports: The port information of the source network.
Destination Networks: The traffic target destination networks.
Destination Ports: The port information of the destination network.
Protocols: The protocol used for traffic transportation.
Rule Action: The action to be triggered when the traffic matches the rule (Allow or Block).
Status: The status of the configured rule (Enabled or Disabled).
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Edit an access policy rule.
Delete an access policy rule.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.
Go to the IP Address Object page to view and manage IP-based objects.
Go to the IdP Attribute Object page to view and manage IdP-based objects.
